job.title: Field Service Engineer
job.description:
The Company

Our client is a global leader in sensor-based ore sorting and magnetic separation technology, delivering innovative solutions to the mining and resource sectors. With a strong reputation for engineering excellence and cutting-edge technology, they focus on mining operations worldwide to improve operational efficiency, maximise resource recovery, and support more sustainable processing practices

The Opportunity

Reporting to the National Sales Manager, the Field Service Engineer will be responsible for delivering comprehensive after‑sales technical support to customers throughout the full lifecycle of their equipment. This includes installation and commissioning, planned maintenance, unplanned breakdown support, and the programming and optimisation of sorting systems.

After‑sales support may be provided either on site or remotely, including phone-based assistance and remote maintenance access to customer equipment, depending on the situation.

About You

We are seeking an experienced technician who enjoys commissioning new equipment, providing on‑site servicing, delivering technical support, and building strong customer relationships.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate experience in the following areas:
  • Strong electrical expertise, particularly in electrical control systems. A technical degree or diploma in an electrical discipline is highly regarded.
  • Proven fault‑finding and diagnostic skills, with hands‑on experience responding to and resolving breakdown situations.
  • Solid mechanical knowledge, with the ability to work confidently across electrical and mechanical systems.
  • Willingness and ability to travel regularly, sometimes at short notice, including international travel to Germany, the USA, New Zealand, and South East Asia.
  • Flexibility to work outside standard business hours on occasion, including weekends, as operational requirements demand with overtime rates provided.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to clearly explain technical issues to internal teams and customers alike, ensuring expectations are effectively manage
Why This Role

The successful candidate will be provided an excellent compensation package including international training (Germany) and career growth.

Interested candidates are encouraged to apply via the “Apply for this job” button or through our website at www.beilbydt.com.au, quoting reference number 1019474. For further inquiries, please contact Aaron Hooper at ahooper@beilbydt.com.au

job.title: National Account Coordinator
job.description:
The Company

Our client is a leading national organisation with operations spanning Australia and New Zealand. Recognised for its commitment to customer service, operational excellence and strong workplace culture, the business supports a diverse customer base through an extensive network and collaborative service model.

With a strong focus on building long-term customer relationships, the organisation prides itself on delivering responsive solutions, maintaining high service standards and empowering employees to make a genuine impact. Due to a temporary resourcing requirement, an opportunity now exists for a National Account Coordinator to join the team.

The Opportunity

This is a full-time Monday to Friday position within a busy National Account Service team, acting as the primary point of contact for designated customers and supporting Account Managers with customer service and administration activities.

You will be responsible for coordinating customer enquiries, processing requests, preparing quotations, managing order requirements and liaising with internal stakeholders to ensure a consistently high level of service delivery.
The role offers flexibility around start and finish times and, following the completion of initial onboarding and training, the opportunity to work from home several days per week.

About You

We are seeking a proactive and customer-focused professional with the following skills and attributes:
  • Experience in customer service, sales administration, account coordination or business administration
  • Previous experience working within a B2B environment
  • Strong relationship-building and stakeholder management skills
  • Excellent verbal and written communication abilities
  • High attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy
  • Ability to manage competing priorities within a fast-paced environment
  • Strong customer service focus and problem-solving capability
  • Intermediate Microsoft Office skills, including Excel, Word and Outlook
  • Experience using Salesforce, Smartsheet or similar business systems
  • A professional, collaborative and team-oriented approach.
A Certificate IV in Business Administration will be highly regarded.

Why This Role

This opportunity offers an immediate start with a respected national organisation, a supportive team environment and genuine flexibility.

In addition to a competitive hourly rate of $42 per hour plus superannuation, you'll enjoy full-time hours, flexible working arrangements and the ability to work from home following training.

If you enjoy building relationships, delivering outstanding customer service and supporting national customers within a collaborative environment, we would love to hear from you.

For a confidential discussion, contact Jessica O'Neill at Beilby Downing Teal on 0457 336 833. Applications can be submitted via our website.

job.title: Chief Executive Officer - City of Kalgoorlie-Boulder
job.description:
THE CITY
  
The City of Kalgoorlie-Boulder is a modern, thriving regional City located approximately 600km East of Perth. With over 30,000 people living in the City, Kalgoorlie-Boulder combines the welcoming and community-focused attributes of a regional community with the amenities and facilities of a metropolitan City. As the heart of the Goldfields, Kalgoorlie-Boulder is the strategic link between the east-west and north-south infrastructure corridors and has a unique and celebrated heritage, stemming from the gold rush of the 1890s. The City is home to the richest square mile of gold in the world, with a multitude of mining and processing companies operating in the area. There is also a strong local business community that helps support a thriving tourist economy.
  
THE ROLE
  
The Chief Executive Officer will provide strong, engaging leadership to the organisation and community, working with Council to deliver strategic priorities, sound governance and sustainable services that support the City’s mission to “work together for the place and people we call home”. The role is responsible for connecting the community, Council and organisation through effective planning, ensuring legislative compliance, providing timely and accurate advice, developing a capable workforce, supporting long-term financial sustainability, and role modelling ethical, values-led behaviour.
  
REQUIREMENTS
  
The City is seeking a strategic and values-led CEO, preferably with experience at the Executive level within Local Government, who can build alignment around a shared vision. Clear, consistent and engaging leadership is essential, as is fostering trust and connection across the organisation and community. The ideal candidate will be commercially astute, with strong financial capability and a disciplined approach to good governance, along with the ability to mentor, empower and cultivate a high-performing executive team. Your ability to balance immediate priorities with a long-term approach will ensure success in this role.
  
THE PACKAGE
  
The Total Reward Package will be between $298,832 to $455,071 in accordance with the Salaries and Allowances Tribunal Band 1 which is inclusive of base salary, superannuation and a vehicle or vehicle allowance and associated FBT. In addition, flexible benefits including regional allowance, and professional development, are negotiable.
  
The City welcomes applications from accomplished leaders who are interested in becoming an integral part of its regional community and who would like to reside in the region and embrace the lifestyle and opportunities it offers. To support this, suitable housing will be provided as part of the employment contract, enabling the successful applicant to live locally and engage fully with the community they serve.
  
  
HOW TO APPLY
  
To apply please click the Apply Now button or visit www.beilbydt.com.au quoting reference 1119260. Please provide:
  
1. A comprehensive resume; and
2. A three-page document comprising: a one page cover letter providing an overview of your skills, experience and motivation for applying; and two pages addressing the essential selection criteria found within the Application Pack.
  
Download an Application Pack by clicking or copying and pasting this link in your browser: https://beilbydt.com.au/application-packs
  
For initial enquiries, or for any assistance you may need in making your application, please contact Emily Bulloch for a confidential discussion on 0427 582 402 or ebulloch@beilbydt.com.au.
  
Applications will close at 4pm AWST on Monday 21 September 2026.
  
Canvassing of Elected Members will disqualify.

job.title: Steel Detailer (All Experience Levels)
job.description:

Due to continued growth, our client is seeking motivated individuals to join their team in Steel Frame and Truss Detailing. Whether you are an experienced Detailer looking for your next opportunity, a Draftsperson seeking to develop specialised industry skills, or someone with a strong technical aptitude looking to enter the field, this role offers the chance to contribute to a well-established and respected business.

Working alongside a highly experienced team, you will be involved in the preparation of detailed designs and drawings for steel frame and truss projects. The company is committed to supporting professional development, providing structured training where required and opportunities to continually expand your technical capabilities.

Key Responsibilities
  • Prepare and review detailed drawings and plans for steel frame and truss structures
  • Interpret architectural and engineering drawings, specifications and project requirements
  • Collaborate with project managers, builders and internal stakeholders to ensure project accuracy and delivery outcomes
  • Utilise industry specific detailing and drafting software
  • Ensure drawings comply with relevant standards and project requirements
  • Contribute to project documentation and continuous improvement initiatives
About You
 
Applications are welcomed from candidates with varying levels of experience. You may bring:
  • Experience in steel detailing, drafting, design or a related technical discipline; or
  • Qualifications or studies in engineering, drafting, design, construction or a similar field; or
  • Strong technical aptitude with a genuine interest in building a career within the steel and construction industry.
In addition, you will ideally possess: 
  • Strong attention to detail and problem-solving skills
  • Excellent communication and teamwork abilities

Why This Role 
  • Permanent opportunities
  • Comprehensive training program with ongoing mentorship
  • Competitive remuneration with potential for salary progression
  • Supportive and collaborative team environment
  • Long-term career development and advancement opportunities
Please apply via the Apply for this job button or online at www.beilbydt.com.au, quoting job reference 1245294.

For initial enquiries or assistance with your application, please contact Jessica O’Neill on 0457 336 833.

job.title: Operations Manager
job.description:
The Company

Northern Australia Civil is a privately owned civil services business operating throughout the Northern Territory and Western Australia.  The business provides wet hire plant and skilled labour solutions to civil, mining and infrastructure clients, while also delivering selected civil contracting works including mine site development, road construction, bulk earthworks, drainage and remote infrastructure.

With a reputation built on quality, reliability and strong client relationships, NAC has continued to grow across Northern Australia. The company’s fleet, workforce and project capability support principal contractors across challenging regional and remote environments, with a strong focus on safe, reliable and productive delivery.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the Managing Director, the Operations Manager will lead the day-to-day delivery of plant and labour hire operations across multiple client sites throughout NT and WA.

The role is responsible for coordinating plant, operators and labour resources, ensuring client commitments are delivered safely, efficiently and to a high standard. You will also support selected civil projects and drive improvements in planning, utilisation and operational performance.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Lead plant and labour hire operations across NT and WA , with travel to sites required
  • Coordinate workforce rosters, plant allocation and mobilisation
  • Manage client delivery requirements and operational issues
  • Improve scheduling, resource utilisation and operational systems
  • Lead supervisors, operators, labour hire personnel and project teams
  • Monitor utilisation, productivity and operational costs
  • Support safety, quality and compliance standards
  • Liaise with the NAC workshop regarding servicing, repairs and workforce allocation
About You

You are an experienced operational leader with a background in plant hire, labour hire, civil construction, mining or a similar industry. You bring strong commercial awareness, practical leadership skills and the ability to coordinate people, equipment and clients across multiple sites.
  
Ideally, you will have:
  • Experience in a senior operational leadership role
  • Proven ability to coordinate plant, equipment and workforce resources
  • Strong understanding of utilisation, service delivery and cost control
  • Excellent planning, organisation and problem-solving skills
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management capability
  • Good Microsoft Office skills
  • Current C Class Driver Licence and White Card
Experience in wet hire, labour hire or civil operations is key to this role. Qualifications in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Business, Logistics or a related field will be well regarded although your years of experience and leadership skills will be equally well regarded

Why This Role

This is an opportunity to play a key leadership role within a growing business that has established civil contracting capability and a strong reputation across Northern Australia.

You will have the autonomy to lead operations, improve performance, support a capable team and contribute directly to the company's continued growth.

 For further information, please contact Mark Turner on 0401 404 451.

job.title: Engineering Manager
job.description:
The Company

Our client is a well-established and highly regarded Australian manufacturer operating a large-scale production facility in Western Australia. With a strong focus on safety, innovation and operational excellence, the business supplies critical products to customers across Australia and has built a reputation for quality, reliability and continuous improvement.
The organisation continues to invest in its people, technology and manufacturing capability to maintain its market-leading position and support future growth. As part of this commitment, a key opportunity has arisen for an experienced Engineering Manager to lead the engineering and maintenance function, driving plant performance, reliability and capital project delivery across a complex manufacturing operation.
This is an opportunity to join a values-driven business where engineering plays a critical role in operational success, and where a proactive leader can make a genuine impact on performance, culture and long-term business outcomes.

The Opportunity

Reporting directly to the General Manager Manufacturing, this is a key leadership position responsible for driving engineering excellence across a large-scale manufacturing operation.
Leading a skilled engineering and maintenance team, you will be responsible for plant reliability, preventative maintenance strategies, capital project delivery, asset lifecycle management and continuous improvement initiatives. This role provides the opportunity to influence operational performance, embed best practice engineering standards and play a pivotal role in supporting the future growth of the business.
This is an outstanding opportunity for an experienced engineering leader who enjoys balancing strategic planning with hands-on operational support in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead and implement the site's engineering strategy with a strong focus on quality, cost, delivery and operational performance.
  • Drive a preventative maintenance and continuous improvement culture to maximise equipment reliability and availability.
  • Lead and develop the engineering and maintenance team, providing coaching, technical guidance and succession planning.
  • Monitor plant and equipment performance, identifying opportunities to improve reliability and efficiency.
  • Reduce downtime and improve maintenance outcomes through effective planning and asset management practices.
  • Continue the implementation and optimisation of SAP maintenance systems and reporting.
  • Develop and manage critical spare parts strategies to support operational requirements.
  • Deliver capital investment projects from concept through to commissioning.
  • Manage engineering budgets, maintenance expenditure and financial reporting.
  • Partner closely with production teams to coordinate maintenance activities and support operational objectives.
  • Drive innovation and continuous improvement initiatives across the manufacturing facility.
  • Ensure compliance with all safety, contractor management and high-risk work requirements.
About You

You are a degree-qualified engineering professional with a proven track record leading engineering and maintenance functions within a large-scale manufacturing environment.
You bring strong technical expertise, commercial acumen and a passion for continuous improvement. Equally comfortable in the boardroom and on the factory floor, you are a collaborative leader who can engage stakeholders, build capability within teams and deliver sustainable operational improvements.
Your experience includes leading preventative maintenance programs, capital project delivery, asset management and the implementation of maintenance systems that improve plant reliability and business performance.

You Will Demonstrate
  • Degree qualifications in Engineering.
  • Minimum five years' experience in an engineering maintenance leadership role within a manufacturing environment.
  • Proven ability to lead, coach and develop high-performing technical teams.
  • Experience implementing preventative and planned maintenance programs.
  • Strong asset reliability and maintenance management expertise.
  • Hands-on experience with SAP or similar CMMS/ERP systems.
  • Demonstrated project management and capital delivery experience.
  • Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting capability.
  • Strong communication, stakeholder engagement and influencing skills.
  • Budget management and financial reporting capability.
  • Sound knowledge of workplace health and safety requirements.
  • A proactive, results-driven approach with a strong focus on continuous improvement.
Why This Role

This is an opportunity to join a highly successful Australian manufacturer with a strong reputation, significant market presence and ongoing commitment to investment and innovation.
You'll have the autonomy to influence engineering strategy, drive meaningful operational improvements and lead a critical function within the business. Working closely with senior leadership, you'll play a key role in shaping plant performance, developing people and delivering projects that contribute directly to the long-term success of the organisation.
For an engineering leader seeking a rewarding role with genuine impact, this represents an exceptional career opportunity.

To Apply

Please apply via the “Apply for this job” button or online at www.beilbydt.com.au quoting reference number 1125112.  For initial enquiries or assistance with your application, please contact Nick Verkerk at nverkerk@beilbydt.com.au

job.title: Chief executive officer - APONT
job.description:
THE ORGANISATION

Aboriginal Peak Organisations Northern Territory (APONT) is an Aboriginal controlled charitable alliance of eight peak Aboriginal organisations. It was created to provide coordinated responses to key issues and concerns of Aboriginal people in the Northern Territory (NT). For 15 years APONT has been instrumental in negotiating new ways forward for NT Aboriginal people and communities by influencing government policy and ways of working. This includes the historic $842.6 million NT Remote Aboriginal Investment partnership agreement signed by APONT, the Commonwealth Government and the Northern Territory Government in February 2025.

THE ROLE

This role is open to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people only. Reporting to, and working closely with the APONT directors, the CEO will continue the organisation’s mandate, to advocate for and advance the rights, health, and livelihoods of Aboriginal people in the NT. The CEO will manage the day-to-day operations and around 15 employees with a key priority of managing grant programs as part of the NT Remote Aboriginal Investment, with $61 million to be delivered directly by APONT over the next five years. The CEO will lead negotiations with all three levels of government and maintain a commitment to leading Aboriginal involvement in policy development and implementation, and to expanding opportunities for Aboriginal community control.

REQUIREMENTS

If you have experience at an executive level in an Aboriginal organisation and experience of managing grants, we would be interested to hear from you. A track record of leading through significant and complex political contexts, change and growth, will be essential, as will a demonstrated understanding of the political, social and Aboriginal context in the NT. High level visionary, strategic and authentic leadership skills will be critical to success in this role.

THE PACKAGE

In return you will receive a three-year contract and a competitive remuneration package of $250,000 plus superannuation and access to salary sacrificing benefits.
To apply please click the Apply Now button or visit www.beilbydt.com.au quoting reference 1133251. Please provide a comprehensive resume together with a one-page covering letter, outlining your interest in the position and addressing your suitability to the role.

Download an Application Pack here: https://beilbydt.com.au/application-packs

For initial enquiries, or for any assistance you may need in making your application, please contact Emily Bulloch for a confidential discussion on 0427 582 402 or ebulloch@beilbydt.com.au.
Applications will close at 5.30pm ACST on Friday 11 September 2026.
The filling of this position is intended to constitute a special/equal opportunity measure under s8(1) of the Racial Discrimination Act 1975 (Cth), and s57 of the Anti-Discrimination Act 1996 (NT).

job.title: Branch Manager

job.title: Senior Director
job.description:

The Department of the Premier and Cabinet supports the Premier as head of the Western Australian Government. The Department is a central agency that leads the public sector in providing advice and support to the Premier and Cabinet in their service of the Western Australian Community. They foster a workplace culture based on their core values, Leadership, Connection and Impact. For more information about the Department, please visit their website. 
The Office of Digital Government (DGov) is leading the digital transformation of the WA public sector to support agencies in improving service delivery to the community. Ensuring that information and data collected, stored and shared by the WA Government is protected and used to improve better outcomes for the community is a crucial element of what they do. The Digital Transformation and Technology Business Unit (DTT) is responsible for the development, operation and governance of whole‑of‑government digital assets and platforms that support digital service delivery to the community. 

About the Role

The Senior Director provides leadership across strategy, product development, user experience, governance, implementation, and operation of digital services to WA citizens, businesses and communities. This role is critical in ensuring a centralised and coordinated approach for DTT. If you are passionate about supporting an efficient public sector and can see how your leadership and expertise can facilitate a wide range of agencies delivering meaningful services for Western Australian’s then we encourage you to apply. 

For further job related information:

job.title: Business Development Manager
job.description:
The Company

Established in 1992, our client has built a standout reputation for delivering high‑quality signage at competitive prices.
For more than 30 years, their expert team of sign makers has helped businesses across Perth and throughout Australia elevate their brand and stand out from the crowd. By designing and custom‑crafting signage that boosts visibility, they help clients present as businesses people want to shop with, buy from, dine at, or engage with.
What truly sets them apart is their end‑to‑end approach. From creative design through to manufacture and professional installation, the entire sign‑making process is handled in‑house. This is made possible by their exceptionally talented design team and fully qualified sign makers, ensuring quality, consistency, and attention to detail at every stage.
  
The Opportunity

Reporting to the Managing Director, the Business Development Manager will be responsible for hunting and generating new business by building and managing a structured prospecting plan, with a strong focus on outbound activity, client meetings, and site visits. The role owns opportunities end-to-end, qualifying leads against capability, timelines and margin targets, and progressing proposals through to signed purchase orders.
Alongside business growth, the role is responsible for managing and growing an assigned customer portfolio, maintaining regular call cycles, running quarterly reviews, and protecting margin through disciplined scope and variation control.

About You

We are looking for a driven sales professional who loves the chase, enjoys opening new doors, and has the following skills to succeed in the role:
  • Proven strength across prospecting, discovery, negotiation, and deal closure.
  • Solid estimating capability, including take-offs, cost modelling, margin calculations, and hands-on (signage knowledge – preferred).
  • Advanced Excel skills with disciplined document control using SharePoint.
  • Confident communicator with both production teams and customers, including the ability to clearly manage scope boundaries and variations.
  • Highly organised, able to juggle multiple active quotes, customers, and follow-ups while protecting margin.
Why This Role

The successful candidate will be provided support and mentoring to succeed, plus be rewarded with an excellent compensation package including Uncapped Commission and Car Allowance.

Interested candidates are encouraged to apply via the “Apply for this job” button or through our website at www.beilbydt.com.au, quoting reference number 1131511 . For further inquiries, please contact Aaron Hooper at ahooper@beilbydt.com.au

job.title: WHS Advisor
job.description:
The Company

Our client is a well-established and globally connected organisation operating across manufacturing, warehousing and distribution environments throughout Australia and New Zealand. Recognised for its commitment to quality, innovation and operational excellence, the business continues to invest in its people, systems and workplace safety practices to support long-term growth and sustainability.

Safety is a core organisational value, with a genuine commitment to creating healthy, safe and supportive workplaces for employees, contractors and visitors. With multiple operating entities and sites, the organisation is focused on driving consistency in safety practices, strengthening safety leadership and continuously improving performance across all areas of the business.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the Head of HSE, the WHS Advisor will be responsible for delivering health, safety and wellbeing initiatives across several operational sites. Acting as a trusted advisor to leaders and employees, you will provide practical safety guidance, coaching and support while helping maintain a strong culture of compliance and continuous improvement.

Key result areas include incident management, injury management and return to work coordination, facilitating safety training and awareness programs, conducting risk assessments and audits, maintaining WHS systems and documentation, and ensuring compliance with legislative obligations and organisational standards. The role will also contribute to harmonising safety practices across multiple businesses and supporting a broader health and wellbeing agenda.

Critical to the position is the ability to build strong working relationships with operational leaders and employees, influence positive safety behaviours and provide practical solutions that improve workplace health and safety outcomes. This role offers significant variety and the opportunity to make a visible impact across multiple sites and business functions.

About You

We are seeking an engaging and proactive safety professional with the following skills and attributes:
  • Experience within manufacturing, warehousing, construction or a similar operational environment
  • Qualifications in Workplace Health and Safety (Cert IV WHS or higher) or currently working towards formal qualifications
  • Demonstrated experience in a health and safety focused role
  • Strong understanding of risk management, incident investigation and injury management processes
  • Experience facilitating training, presentations or educational sessions
  • Proven ability to build productive relationships with stakeholders at all levels
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Highly organised with excellent time management and prioritisation skills
  • Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office capability
Why This Role

This is an excellent opportunity to join a respected organisation that genuinely values safety, employee wellbeing and continuous improvement. You will be given the opportunity to work closely with experienced leaders, influence safety outcomes across multiple operational environments and contribute to meaningful initiatives that protect and support people at work.

The role offers diversity, autonomy and the chance to make a tangible difference within a growing business. If you enjoy partnering with people, building capability and driving positive safety outcomes, this position provides an outstanding platform to further develop your career while contributing to a high-performing organisation.

For a confidential discussion, contact Jessica O'Neill on 0457 336 833. Applications should be submitted via Beilby Downing Teal.
